cohorts.name: Gastrointestinal Inflammation / Bleeding Pattern
cohorts.description: Blood or inflammatory cells in the stool, usually alongside systemic markers of inflammation and anaemia.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The Disease Master IBD row lists 'Stool analysis (occult blood), CBC, inflammatory markers' - a marker set that spans three profiles and cannot be evaluated from Stool Analysis alone.

triggers.label: White cells present in stool - invasive or inflammatory process

supporting.label: Anaemia - chronic blood loss or inflammation
Albumin low - protein-losing enteropathy or chronic inflammation
Reactive thrombocytosis - common in active bowel inflammation

evidence.citation: Lamb CA et al., BSG Consensus Guidelines on the Management of IBD in Adults, Gut 2019;68(s3):s1-s106
evidence.note: Raised CRP, anaemia, thrombocytosis and low albumin as markers of active bowel inflammation; faecal calprotectin distinguishes IBD from IBS.

evidence.citation: Lacy BE et al., ACG Clinical Guideline: Management of Irritable Bowel Syndrome, Am J Gastroenterol 2021;116:17-44
evidence.note: IBS is a positive symptom-based diagnosis requiring the absence of alarm features and normal inflammatory markers.

diseases.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn's Disease/Ulcerative Colitis)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Persistent diarrhea (over several weeks) with blood/mucus, unexplained weight loss, abnormal stool findings with systemic symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: Stool analysis (occult blood), CBC, inflammatory markers

diseases.name: Bacterial Gastroenteritis (Salmonella/Shigella)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Acute bloody or high-volume diarrhea with fever'; Related Markers/Tests: Stool analysis (microscopy for white/red blood cells)

diseases.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Chronic pattern fits symptom-based criteria AND stool/blood tests show NO red-flag findings' - this cohort's findings argue against IBS rather than for it

diseases.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
diseases.dm_basis: Cross-linked because gastrointestinal blood loss is the leading cause of iron deficiency in adult men and postmenopausal women

diseases.name: Celiac Disease
diseases.dm_basis: Related Profile(s) on the Celiac Disease row includes Stool Analysis

cohorts.name: Intestinal Parasite Detection
cohorts.description: Ova, cysts or parasites seen on stool microscopy.

triggers.label: Ova, cysts or parasites seen on stool microscopy

supporting.label: Anaemia - hookworm and other parasites cause chronic blood loss

evidence.citation: WHO Guideline: Preventive Chemotherapy to Control Soil-Transmitted Helminth Infections, 2017
evidence.note: Stool microscopy as the standard field diagnostic; anaemia and eosinophilia as associated findings.

diseases.name: Intestinal Parasitic Infection
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Ova, cysts, or parasites identified on stool microscopy, especially with compatible symptoms or exposure history'; Related Markers/Tests: Stool microscopy/ova and parasite exam

diseases.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
diseases.dm_basis: Cross-linked because intestinal parasites are a leading cause of iron deficiency where they are endemic

cohorts.name: Abnormal Semen Parameters
cohorts.description: Sperm concentration, motility or morphology below the WHO lower reference limits.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: Hormone parameters are admitted as supporting signals because the Disease Master Male Hypogonadism row lists 'Testosterone, LH, FSH, Semen Analysis parameters' together.

triggers.label: Sperm concentration below the WHO lower reference limit of 16 million/mL
Total motility below the WHO lower reference limit of 42%
Progressive motility below the WHO lower reference limit of 30%
Normal morphology below the WHO lower reference limit of 4%

supporting.label: Semen volume below the WHO lower reference limit of 1.4 mL
Sperm concentration below 1 million/mL - severe oligozoospermia or azoospermia
Prolactin raised - suppresses the gonadal axis

evidence.citation: WHO Laboratory Manual for the Examination and Processing of Human Semen, 6th edition, 2021
evidence.note: Lower reference limits (5th centile): volume 1.4 mL, concentration 16 million/mL, total motility 42%, progressive motility 30%, normal forms 4%.

evidence.citation: Schlegel PN et al., AUA/ASRM Guideline: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men, Fertil Steril 2021;115:54-61
evidence.note: Two abnormal semen analyses before diagnosis; endocrine evaluation when concentration is low or there are clinical features of hypogonadism.

diseases.name: Male Infertility (Oligospermia/Azoospermia)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Sperm concentration below the reference range on semen analysis, especially on repeat testing'; Related Markers/Tests: Semen analysis (sperm count/concentration)

diseases.name: Asthenozoospermia (Reduced Sperm Motility)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Motile sperm percentage below the reference range on semen analysis, especially on repeat testing'; Related Markers/Tests: Semen analysis (sperm motility)

diseases.name: Varicocele-related Infertility
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Abnormal semen analysis with a palpable scrotal varicocele on examination' - the examination finding is not lab-derivable, so weight is limited

diseases.name: Male Hypogonadism
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: 'Testosterone, LH, FSH, Semen Analysis parameters'

cohorts.name: Genital Tract Infection Pattern
cohorts.description: Bacterial growth on semen culture, or excess leukocytes in semen.

triggers.label: Semen culture shows significant bacterial growth
Leukocytes in semen above 1 million/mL - leukocytospermia

supporting.label: Reduced motility - infection impairs sperm function

evidence.citation: Bonkat G et al., EAU Guidelines on Urological Infections, 2023
evidence.note: Bacterial prostatitis and epididymo-orchitis: culture-based diagnosis, with sexually transmitted pathogens predominating in younger men.

diseases.name: Bacterial Prostatitis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive bacterial growth on semen culture with matching sensitivity profile'; Related Markers/Tests: Semen culture and sensitivity, Primary smear of semen

diseases.name: Epididymitis/Epididymo-orchitis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive bacterial growth on semen/urine culture with matching clinical presentation'; Related Markers/Tests: Semen culture and sensitivity

diseases.name: Chlamydia
diseases.dm_basis: Cross-linked because chlamydia is a leading cause of epididymitis in younger men

cohorts.name: Neuro-Autoimmune Serology
cohorts.description: A positive neurological autoantibody or a raised CSF protein - findings that always require neurology interpretation alongside the clinical picture.

supporting.label: B12 deficient - a reversible contributor to neurological symptoms that should be corrected regardless

evidence.citation: Gilhus NE et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers 2019;5:30
evidence.note: AChR antibodies are present in roughly 85% of generalised myasthenia gravis and are highly specific.

evidence.citation: Wingerchuk DM et al., Neurology 2015;85:177-89
evidence.note: International consensus criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder based on AQP4-IgG serostatus.

evidence.citation: Leonhard SE et al., Nat Rev Neurol 2019;15:671-83
evidence.note: Guillain-Barre syndrome: albuminocytologic dissociation - raised CSF protein with a normal cell count.

evidence.citation: Graus F et al., Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404
evidence.note: Clinical approach to autoimmune encephalitis and the interpretation of neuronal antibody panels.

diseases.name: Myasthenia Gravis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive AChR antibody with fatigable muscle weakness'; Related Markers/Tests: AChR (Acetylcholine Receptor) Antibodies

diseases.name: Multiple Sclerosis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive Anti-MOG or Anti-NMO/Aquaporin4 with matching neurological symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: Anti-MOG, Anti-Aquaporin4 (NMO), CSF Proteins

diseases.name: Guillain-Barre Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated CSF protein with normal cell count following recent infection, with progressive weakness'; Severity/Urgency: 'Emergency - can progress to respiratory failure within days'

diseases.name: Autoimmune/Paraneoplastic Encephalitis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive paraneoplastic antibody panel (Hu/Ri/Amphiphysin/CASPR2/AMPA) with matching neuro-psychiatric symptoms'

cohorts.name: Peripheral Neuropathy Risk Pattern
cohorts.description: The two commonest metabolic causes of peripheral neuropathy - B12 deficiency and sustained hyperglycaemia - detected together.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The Disease Master Peripheral Neuropathy row is itself tagged to all three of these profiles and lists 'Vitamin B12, HbA1c/Fasting Glucose (cross-link Diabetes)'. This cohort implements that cross-link directly.

triggers.label: Vitamin B12 in the deficient range
HbA1c at or above 7% - sustained hyperglycaemia
Fasting glucose in the diabetic range

supporting.label: HbA1c at or above 9% - markedly raised, higher neuropathy risk
Reduced eGFR - uraemic neuropathy is an additional contributor

evidence.citation: Pop-Busui R et al., Diabetic Neuropathy: A Position Statement by the American Diabetes Association, Diabetes Care 2017;40:136-54
evidence.note: Glycaemic exposure as the main modifiable driver of distal symmetric polyneuropathy; screening recommended at diagnosis in type 2 diabetes.

evidence.citation: Stabler SP, N Engl J Med 2013;368:149-60
evidence.note: B12 deficiency neuropathy can precede haematological changes and may be irreversible if untreated.

diseases.name: Peripheral Neuropathy
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low B12 or poorly controlled diabetes together with sensory symptoms in a stocking-glove pattern'; Related Markers/Tests: Vitamin B12, HbA1c/Fasting Glucose

diseases.name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: Vitamin B12

diseases.name: Diabetes Mellitus
diseases.dm_basis: Possible Complications on the Diabetes Mellitus row include neuropathy

cohorts.name: Antiepileptic Drug Level Monitoring
cohorts.description: A carbamazepine level outside the usual therapeutic window. Monitoring context only - drug levels do not diagnose epilepsy.

triggers.label: Carbamazepine level outside the usual therapeutic range of 4-12 ug/mL

supporting.label: Sodium low - carbamazepine is a recognised cause of hyponatraemia
Leukopenia - a known haematological effect of carbamazepine

evidence.citation: Patsalos PN et al., ILAE Position Paper on Antiepileptic Drug Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, Epilepsia 2008;49:1239-76
evidence.note: Reference ranges are guides; clinical response takes precedence over the number.

evidence.citation: Van Amelsvoort T et al., Epilepsia 1994;35:181-8
evidence.note: Carbamazepine-induced hyponatraemia as a dose-related adverse effect.

diseases.name: Epilepsy
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Recurrent unprovoked seizures confirmed on EEG; drug levels used for monitoring, not diagnosis'; Related Markers/Tests: Carbamazepine (Tegretol) level for those on treatment. Weight is deliberately limited - the Disease Master states this marker is not diagnostic.

cohorts.name: Raised Tumour Marker
cohorts.description: A tumour marker above its reference value. These are surveillance and monitoring tools; none is diagnostic on its own, and all can be raised in benign conditions.

supporting.label: PSA at or above 10 ng/mL - markedly raised
AFP at or above 200 ng/mL - markedly raised

evidence.citation: Sturgeon CM et al., NACB Laboratory Medicine Practice Guidelines for Use of Tumor Markers, Clin Chem 2008;54:e11-79
evidence.note: Tumour markers lack the specificity for diagnosis; their validated roles are surveillance, prognosis and treatment monitoring.

evidence.citation: Wei JT et al., AUA/SUO Guideline: Early Detection of Prostate Cancer, J Urol 2023;210:46-53
evidence.note: PSA thresholds and the need for confirmation and shared decision-making before biopsy.

evidence.citation: Marrero JA et al., AASLD Guidance on Hepatocellular Carcinoma, Hepatology 2018;68:723-50
evidence.note: AFP with ultrasound for surveillance in chronic liver disease; AFP alone is insufficient.

diseases.name: Prostate Cancer
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated/rising PSA, especially with abnormal digital rectal exam'; Related Markers/Tests: PSA. Weight is capped because the Disease Master indicator also requires an examination finding.

diseases.name: Ovarian Cancer
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated tumor marker with imaging findings suspicious for a mass'; Related Markers/Tests: CA-125. Weight is capped because imaging is required.

diseases.name: Breast Cancer
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Palpable mass or imaging finding with abnormal biopsy result'; Related Markers/Tests: 'Tumor markers if included in panel (e.g., CA 15-3)'. Weight is low - the Disease Master makes clear the marker is not the screening test.

diseases.name: Pancreatic Cancer
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'New unexplained jaundice/weight loss with elevated tumor marker and imaging findings'; Related Markers/Tests: Amylase, CA 19-9

diseases.name: Liver Cancer (Hepatocellular Carcinoma)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Rising or markedly elevated AFP in a patient with chronic liver disease or a liver mass on imaging'; Related Markers/Tests: Alfa Feto Protein (AFP), LFT markers

cohorts.name: Lymphoproliferative Screening Pattern
cohorts.description: Raised LDH with lymphocyte abnormality and cytopenias - a combination that warrants haematology review for a lymphoproliferative process.

evidence.citation: Cheson BD et al., Recommendations for Initial Evaluation, Staging, and Response Assessment of Lymphoma (Lugano Classification), J Clin Oncol 2014;32:3059-68
evidence.note: LDH as a prognostic marker requiring tissue diagnosis for confirmation.

evidence.citation: Swerdlow SH et al., Blood 2016;127:2375-90
evidence.note: WHO classification of lymphoid neoplasms; peripheral blood findings as an initial trigger for further investigation.

diseases.name: Lymphoma (Suspected/Screening)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Persistent unexplained lymphadenopathy with elevated LDH and systemic symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: CBC, LDH. Weight is capped because lymphadenopathy - the central finding - is not lab-derivable.

diseases.name: Leukemia (Suspected/Screening)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Markedly abnormal WBC count with abnormal differential, especially with low hemoglobin and platelets together'

diseases.name: Multiple Myeloma
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators reference anaemia and hypercalcaemia within the CRAB pattern

cohorts.name: Prostate-Specific Antigen Elevation
cohorts.description: PSA above the commonly used threshold. Benign prostatic enlargement, prostatitis and recent instrumentation all raise PSA.

supporting.label: Semen culture positive - prostatitis can raise PSA and should be treated before re-testing
Urine culture positive - infection can raise PSA

evidence.citation: Wei JT et al., AUA/SUO Guideline: Early Detection of Prostate Cancer, J Urol 2023;210:46-53
evidence.note: PSA thresholds, confirmatory repeat testing and shared decision-making before biopsy.

evidence.citation: Nadler RB et al., J Urol 1995;154:407-13
evidence.note: Inflammation and benign enlargement as non-malignant causes of PSA elevation.

diseases.name: Prostate Cancer
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated/rising PSA, especially with abnormal digital rectal exam'; Related Markers/Tests: PSA (Prostate-Specific Antigen, if included in panel)

diseases.name: Bacterial Prostatitis
diseases.dm_basis: Cross-linked as a benign cause of PSA elevation that the Disease Master covers under Semen Culture and Sensitivity
